questions.question: Explain what the Renaissance was and where it began.
questions.expected_answer: The Renaissance, which means rebirth, was a period of great flowering of art, learning and new ideas in Europe, especially in the 1400s and 1500s. It began in Italy, particularly in the rich city of Florence, and spread across Europe. Scholars studied the learning of ancient Greece and Rome, much of it kept and developed by Arab and Byzantine scholars, and rich patrons such as the Medici family supported artists and scholars.

questions.question: Describe two new ideas or inventions of the Renaissance.
questions.expected_answer: Artists used perspective and light and shadow to make paintings look real, and studied the human body. Gutenberg's printing press with movable metal letters, developed in Germany around the 1440s and 1450s, allowed books to be printed quickly and cheaply, spreading ideas widely. Humanism valued human abilities and education.

questions.question: Why is the Renaissance seen as a turning point, and how did it encourage exploration?
questions.expected_answer: More people began to question old ideas, observe carefully and test ideas, which was the beginning of modern science, as when Copernicus argued in 1543 that the Earth moves around the sun. This curiosity and confidence made people want to know what lay beyond their maps. Better star measurements helped sailors, printed maps spread new knowledge, and rulers and merchants paid for voyages.
